\begin{bankq}[id=SA01-P2-MATH-S1-Q07, source={Score Advanced - Test 01 (22 Sep 2020)}, paper=2, qno=7, type=multi, subtopic={Position vectors}, answer={B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S1 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: distances from the centroid, position vectors | steps: Leibniz relation; sum of squares}]

Consider a parallelogram ABCD. A straight line is drawn which cuts AB, AC, AD at points P, Q, R respectively. If $\overrightarrow{\text{AP}}$ = $\alpha\overrightarrow{\text{AB}}$, $\overrightarrow{\text{AR}}$ = $\beta\overrightarrow{\text{AD}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\text{AQ}}$ = $\dfrac{\gamma}{2}\overrightarrow{\text{AC}}$ where $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ are positive scalars, then
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ are in A.P.}
\opt{B}{$\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ are in H.P.}
\opt{C}{$\alpha$, $\gamma$, $\beta$ are in H.P.}
\opt{D}{$\alpha\beta\geq\gamma^2$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS04-P1-MATH-S3-Q04, source={TMAS - Test 04 (19 Nov 2023)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Position vectors}, answer={4.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: vector identity of a quadrilateral | steps: midpoints; expand squares; lambda}]
